parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Two parallel plate capacitors C₁ and C₂ are connected to a supply that has a potential difference (p.d.) Vₛ. The capacitors may be connected in series or in parallel.

The supply provides charge Qₛ and the plates of the two capacitors are charges Q₁ and Q₂ respectively. The p.d.s across the plates of the capacitors are V₁ and V₂ respectively.

Complete Table 6.1 to indicate how Qₛ, Q₁ and Q₂ relate to each other, and how Vₛ, V₁, and V₂ relate to each other, for series and parallel connections of the capacitors to the supply.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: An isolated capacitor of capacitance 470 μF stores 19 mJ of energy.
parts.text: Calculate the p.d. across the capacitor.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the charge on the capacitor.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The capacitor is now connected in parallel with a capacitor of capacitance 180 μF that is initially uncharged.

Determine the total energy, in mJ, now stored in the two capacitors.
